newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Futures Exch focusing on NYMEX, HIBOR contracts.
newsitem.headline: HK Futures Exch focusing on NYMEX, HIBOR contracts.

text.p: Trading in H-share index futures might be possible by the end of the year, the Hong Kong Futures Exchange (HKFE) said on Friday.

But HKFE spokesman Ross Lai said there was no firm date set yet for futures contracts on H-shares -- Hong Kong-listed shares in China-incorporated companies. But he denied a newspaper report of a launch in August.
"It seems that other projects are likely to be launched earlier than(H-share futures)," he said.

Lai said the HKFE was currently working on an electronically traded version of a Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate (HIBOR) futures contract, and a product allowing Hong Kong trading in New York Mercantile Exchange products.
"These two will take precedence over other products," he said.
A local newspaper earlier reported the HKFE was planning an August launch of H-share index contract and a contract based on red chips -- Hong Kong companies with strong mainland ties.
Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) executive David White confirmed that Hang Seng Index Services, who compile Hong benchmark Hang Seng Index, was looking at putting together a red chip index.
"Getting up a new index product is relatively straightforward," said White.
However, the SFC would want to review any new index product submitted to it, White said.
